subject: Request: temporary SLA amendment for filter & tool-call latency impacts
messages:
From: Kerry Liu <kerry.liu@optimahth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Timothy Hale <timothy.hale@optimahth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: SLA amendment for inference pipeline - Optima

Jordan —

Thanks for taking a look. Over the last 10 days we've seen repeated production incidents where our patient triage workflow spikes in latency (3–5x baseline) and occasionally returns malformed JSON from the structured-output route. Our engineering team traced the pattern to the content-filter + tool-call chain: when the filter classifies certain clinical phrases as potential PII, requests are rerouted to a slower tool-calling fallback that also triggers additional validation steps. The net effect is frequent timeout / degraded responses for a subset of prompts that are critical to our SLAs with partner hospitals.

We need two things from Redwood:
- confirmation whether this behavior counts as a service-level failure or a justified exception driven by filtering policies
- a short-term amendment or carve-out to the uptime/latency SLOs while we test a mitigation you propose (we can't change our upstream prompts without risking clinical flow)

I've attached logs and a short sample of failing prompts. Happy to jump on a call — ideally this week.

Attachments: optima-filter-failure-logs.txt

Thanks,
Kerry Liu
Head of Integrations
Optima HealthTech
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kerry Liu <kerry.liu@optimahth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA amendment for inference pipeline - Optima

Kerry —

Appreciate the clear write-up and logs. Sorry you're seeing this in production. High level: content-filtering and tool-call fallbacks are designed to protect downstream integrations, but we haven't seen a case where filtering classification causes repeated structured-output corruption at this scale. We're treating this as urgent.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- I'll open a priority incident with the runtime team (cc'ing Karthik) to reproduce with your logs.
- Can you provide the top 5 failing prompt examples (we'll need exact tokens)? You attached logs — those help but the raw prompts accelerate triage.
- As a contingency we can discuss a temporary SLA amendment that explicitly excludes filter-induced structured-output degradation while we run an account-scoped policy experiment. That amendment would be timeboxed and include increased monitoring and rollback criteria.

Can you do a 30-min slot Wed or Thu? If you prefer a write-up first, send the 5 prompts and we'll sketch the amendment language.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Lead, North America
Redwood Inference
From: Kerry Liu <kerry.liu@optimahth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Timothy Hale <timothy.hale@optimahth.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA amendment for inference pipeline - Optima

On Tue, Nov 3, 2026 at 11:05 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Can you provide the top 5 failing prompt examples (we'll need exact tokens)?

Attaching the CSV with the failing prompts (failed-prompts.csv) — includes the full prompt, timestamp, and request id. A few notes:
- The prompts are not malformed; instead the response path returns a validation error from the structured-output layer after the tool-call fallback completes.
- The incidents correlate strongly with messages containing hospital MRN-like patterns; removing or redacting those tokens in tests eliminates the failure but that's not an option for our runtime integration.

We can do Thu 11:00 PT for a quick call.

Thanks — look forward to a fix.
Kerry
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kerry Liu <kerry.liu@optimahth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA amendment for inference pipeline - Optima

Jordan / Kerry —

Following our call this morning, engineering looked through the traces. Summary and proposed customer-scoped experiment:

Findings:
- The content-filter occasionally tags MRN-like tokens as high-risk, triggering the special tool-call fallback which adds ~120–300ms per token and additional validation steps.
- When the fallback engages, our structured-output verifier runs a stricter schema check post-tooling; in rare cases (race between KV cache expiration + additional validation) the verifier fails with a parsing error.

Proposal (temporary, 30-day):
- Scope: Optima account only.
- Change: enable an account-scoped policy that allows structured-output passthrough for requests that match the failing prompt signature, bypassing the tool-call fallback for those patterns.
- Monitoring: incremental rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback if malformed-output rate increases > 0.5% above baseline or latency increases significantly for other customers.
- SLA amendment: for the 30-day experiment Redwood requests a limited carve-out for latency SLOs and structured-output correctness tied solely to filter-triggered fallbacks for the Optima account. If the experiment causes increased errors beyond the rollback thresholds, Redwood will reimburse proportionate credits per the contract's incident credit formula.

If legal / sales are comfortable with the wording we can ship this as a temporary amendment and operational playbook.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: SLA amendment for inference pipeline - Optima — approval request

Team —

Forwarding the thread with the proposal summarized by Marissa. Requesting approval to proceed with the 30-day, account-scoped policy experiment and the limited SLA carve-out language below. This will be presented to Optima as a timeboxed amendment; legal will issue a short addendum.

Proposed carve-out language (high level):
- Duration: 30 days from activation; automatic termination unless extended in writing.
- Scope: Applies only to Optima HealthTech account and only to requests that would otherwise trigger the content-filter -> tool-call fallback chain.
- Effect: While the experiment is active, Redwood will not count filter-triggered tool-call fallback-induced latency spikes or structured-output validation failures against the standard latency and structured-output correctness SLOs.
- Safeguards: Automated incremental rollout; rollback thresholds (malformed-output rate > 0.5% above baseline OR 95th latency > 2x baseline during experiment); full incident crediting if rollback thresholds are breached and cause customer impact.

Questions for approvals:
1) Legal signoff on carve-out phrasing (Rishi)
2) Sales ok to accept a limited carve-out vs. negotiating credits upfront (Marissa / Karthik)
3) Exec visibility — is the timebox and rollback language acceptable?

Please reply with Approve / Decline / Need changes. If I don't hear back by EOD Thu (11/12) I'll escalate to leadership.

Thanks,
Jordan
Enterprise Lead, North America
Redwood Inference
